name: Flat Earth Firmament Visual Anomaly
scope: Adds one isolated massless visual-only FLAT EARTH [ANOMALY] far beyond the main Solar System: flat world disc, zodiac rim, central world tree with exposed roots, transparent four-sided pyramid firmament, and animated local Sun/Moon on a vertical figure-eight path. No N-body body, gravity source, landing surface, atmosphere, collision shape, or replacement Earth is created.
sandboxParentsValidated: Any currently landed planet/moon supported by the existing surface stack; SOL acceptance focuses Earth, Moon, Mars, Europa, Titan and Triton where landing is already enabled.
sandboxDynamicsPolicy: Preview is render-only. COMMIT inserts the selected existing body definition as a normal gravity source at the live reticle-derived initial state. Compact-object mass is not reduced or clamped for system safety: after COMMIT the existing mutual Newtonian velocity-Verlet N-body integration is authoritative and catastrophic disruption/capture/ejection/collision is allowed where modeled.
sandboxReferenceStatePolicy: Surface COMMIT re-solves the astronomical observer, parent state, body rotation, reticle look vector and orbital-shell intersection at the exact commit instant. The body is inserted on that line of sight with a circular prograde tangent; subsequent motion is entirely live mutual Newtonian N-body evolution.
sandboxPreviewPolicy: PREVIEW remains presentation-only and follows the live landed reticle direction. Asteroids use physical apparent size; compact objects use the same bounded readability proxy family as the existing LAB compact-object renderer. The amber ring remains an aiming aid. Preview geometry never participates in gravity.
flightNavigationPolicy: Gravity solver, velocity-Verlet integrator, ship dynamics, flight computer, FRAME/transit, SOL reference states, planetary rotation, atmospheric optics, landing transitions and takeoff/orbit handoff remain inherited and are not redesigned in 0.1.0.6A.
mobileCachePolicy: Changed shell/style/main/app/renderer/surface-renderer/orbit-sandbox edges are stamped ue0106a3 for Safari/GitHub Pages cache isolation; unchanged validated celestial factory/physics/data/surface-state dependencies retain prior URLs.
surfaceSkySpawnPolicy: Actual landed/on-foot surface only; reference SURFACE SKY observer remains excluded. Reticle must be at or above the local horizon. Current landed body is the insertion parent. Body choices are ASTEROID, NEUTRON STAR, PULSAR and BLACK HOLE. Compact types reuse the existing LAB definitions. NEAR/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH are initial orbital-shell presets; warnings do not prevent destructive compact-object commits.
visualPresencePolicy: Sun position/angular geometry remain authoritative; only display glare/white-core presentation is strengthened and reduced progressively at telescope FOV. Planet/moon orbit polish is rendering-only: higher-quality mip/anisotropic filtering and earlier lazy detail residency, with physical radius, lighting geometry and body state unchanged.
compactObjectSurfacePolicy: Surface astronomy detects black-hole/neutron-star body kinds and reuses createCelestialVisual/updateCelestialVisual from the existing space renderer rather than generic reflective spheres. The compressed surface sky adapts only presentation scale; authoritative physical mass/radius and DETAILS angular-size science remain unchanged.
surfaceParentDestructionPolicy: If live impact/absorption deletes the body hosting the active landed session, Explorer exits the invalid surface renderer/session and returns to the live space state without restoring the destroyed parent. This is recovery from a physically allowed sandbox outcome, not a protective clamp.
flatWorldAnomalyPolicy: Explorer presentation-layer phenomenon injected into the COSMOS registry only. Canonical generated/SOL system body arrays and physics metadata remain unchanged. The anomaly is always identified, navigable through existing COSMOS tools, and frameable with the existing massless observation camera.
flatWorldLightingPolicy: The anomaly uses a dedicated render layer for standard materials and local Sun/Moon/ambient lights. The normal Solar-System Sun/ambient lights remain on their existing layer, so the visual world is illuminated by its own internal luminaries rather than the real Solar-System Sun.
flatWorldPlacementPolicy: Fixed remote free-space position approximately 117 AU from the system barycenter and well off the ecliptic. The normal ship camera far plane does not need to render it from the inner Solar System; COSMOS FRAME/ORBIT recenters the existing massless observation camera on it.
flatWorldPhysicsBoundary: visualOnly=true, gravitySource=false; no physical mass, collision, atmosphere, terrain traversal, landing, or hidden force/time effects.
